title: A bill to amend chapters 83 and 84 of title 5, United States Code, to authorize an increase of the retirement age for members of the Capitol Police.
official_summary:
This act authorizes the Capitol Police Board to increase the mandatory retirement age for a member of the Capitol Police to up to age 62 when the board determines such waiver is in the public interest.

Under current law, members of the Capitol Police are generally subject to mandatory retirement at (1) age 57; or (2) upon completing 20 years of service if the member is older than 57. Previously, a waiver from the board would authorize a member to continue working until age 60.

The act authorizes the board to issue a waiver specifying a retirement age between 57 and 62.

summary.headline: New law lets the Capitol Police Board allow officers to keep working until as late as age 62, up from 60.
summary.what_it_does: Capitol Police officers generally must retire at age 57, or once they finish 20 years of service if they are already older than 57. Before this law, the Capitol Police Board could grant a waiver letting an officer work until age 60. This law lets the board set a retirement age anywhere from 57 to 62 when it decides doing so is in the public interest.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Capitol Police
who_it_affects.how: Officers who receive a waiver from the board may be allowed to keep working up to age 62 instead of a maximum of 60.
The board gains the power to grant waivers setting a retirement age anywhere between 57 and 62.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 29, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
